html:
SMTO-RST-0017 — SMTO couldn't open your saved data safely

GUID: 15838f05-da25-5d4d-b6ef-fe2038380e66
Slug: controller-state-unavailable
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while loading your saved data because something about how it was started isn't safe for that data. Your conversations and settings haven't been changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure only one SMTO is using this data. Stop the installed app, or close any other window running ./startup.sh, then start SMTO again. Two servers writing the same data could overwrite each other's work, so SMTO refuses to start.
  2. If you recently reinstalled SMTO or changed its Python version, run the installer again, then start SMTO. SMTO checks its setup before opening saved data and stops if that setup is unsupported.
  3. If it still stops, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The exact message shows which safety check stopped SMTO.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete the data folder; it holds your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server stopped because a saved-data safety check rejected the current startup (for example another process owns the data folder, or the restored state cannot be safely inspected).

What this means

  • StateUnavailable and related internal boundaries reject incompatible hub/path/phase ownership, live SQL access, fenced records, invalid checkpoint/managed-file evidence or unsupported bootstrap/recovery configuration. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • StateUnavailable and related internal boundaries reject incompatible hub/path/phase ownership, live SQL access, fenced records, invalid checkpoint/managed-file evidence or unsupported bootstrap/recovery configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact internal condition and phase; this broad family does not establish corruption or a disk failure by itself.

How to fix it

  • Read the StateUnavailable message in the Server log or Technical details. Stop any other Server using the same AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR, confirm a supported Python runtime, and use the supported offline recovery tools only if the saved state is actually damaged.
  • Check the Server storage diagnostics and the reported lifecycle, repository path or recovery condition. Preserve committed generations; use supported offline recovery for damaged state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning repository/lifecycle contract is restored, with offline recovery used only when the actual retained-state fault requires it.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
